column1: # The runtime logins of the Cloud database, as data: who they are, what each may do on which table, and their
# server-side deadlines. deploy/sql/harden-runtime-roles.sql writes these same rows in its own @rows block; this
# file states them a second time, independently, and deploy/test/runtime-roles.pg.test.ts holds the catalog the
# script leaves against it. Tab-separated: kind, role, subject, value. A value of "-" is "nothing".
# verbs with subject * is the rule for every table of schema public; a named subject narrows it for that table.
# A table named staff_* that has no row here is refused by the script until it is named.
# schema rows are the schemas a login may use; where a host keeps the search extensions (pg_trgm, btree_gin) in a
# schema of their own, the script adds that one by itself. deadline values are milliseconds.
# The row lock's views. Under the lock a search through public loses its indexes (a policy keeps a condition on an
# index only when its operators are leakproof, and the search's are not), so the search reads three views in schema
# ohmail, each answering the bound account's rows alone. The lock's setup step makes them, owned by the migrator;
# the script grants them only where they stand: view rows are what a login may do on each (read it, nothing more),
# and USAGE on ohmail is written only while one of the login's views stands there (before the setup step, nothing).
# routine rows are the lock's two readers, which every view calls: a login may run them, through PUBLIC's EXECUTE,
# and the script grants none. Anything else in ohmail is refused: another relation, another routine, a write, a
# grant option, and any right of any other role there, by any road: an entry (PUBLIC, the staff role, the plane, a
# host's role) or a membership (pg_read_all_data, pg_write_all_data, or a role that holds one, inherited, one SET
# ROLE away, or a grant of its own away by an ADMIN option). The roles that read every row already (SUPERUSER,
# BYPASSRLS, REPLICATION) are the host's; the script's report names them. The lock's ruling said the logins get no
# USAGE on ohmail; the search ruling changed that one line on purpose, for these views.
